issues.description: The SAS program reads dxbrl.final_10k_withxbrl and dxbrl.raw_extra_footnotes as prepared inputs. The datasheet describes upstream Perl filing extraction, section/float processing, XBRL-US tag construction and manual review/corrections, but those producer programs, correction records and input schemas are not in this release. SEC/LM roots and the SEC public route do not establish equivalent section or raw-tag outputs.

The active SAS body reads/writes dxbrl tables but the release supplies no SAS LIBNAME/autoexec or complete orchestration driver. The Stata preparation code is embedded inside a SAS comment and has no import/handoff program or panel-time declaration for D. operators. The regressions are outside this supplied-preparation target.

The supplied Stata fragment creates scaled variables with the SCall_ prefix, then reads SCnum_tags_notes and SCtagsa_* for differences. The prepared upstream schema, any alias-producing step, import format and panel-time setup are not supplied, so the consumer contract cannot be resolved by guessing. Other consumed fields such as MV, CSHR, XYEAR and XBRL1–3 may be inherited through a.*; their definitions/history remain unverified. SAS also creates separate num_tags_notes_total/num_words_notes_total aggregates while the Stata fragment uses both note-level and total fields; their upstream definitions must be preserved as separate concepts.
The supplied code reads dxbrl.element_typerank.FOOTNOTE_TYPE and RANK to resolve dual-classified footnote elements, but no producer, file path or rank values are supplied.
The existing bounded SAS 9.4 startup probe failed while loading TKELS. This leaves the runtime unverified; it does not establish a missing license or a study-specific incompatibility.

evidence.description: The document embeds substantive SAS data preparation and linking code and describes dxbrl tables as necessary for the final dataset.
evidence.quote:
Files labelled "dxbrl." are necessary to arrive at my final data set. A brief description of each of these files and the source
	of the information (along with any additional needed detail) is provided below. After these descriptions, I provide SAS code
	that details variable construction and the process of linking the various data sets together. See the datasheet description
	for details of when the data was downloaded from the source, keeping in mind that variable definitions and labels change
	over time.

evidence.description: The prepared SEC/XBRL table documents an upstream Perl extraction workflow, including HTML cleanup and a four-round section-selection procedure.
evidence.quote:
dxbrl.final_10k_withxbrl - Provides SEC filing information and XBRL information for 10-K and variations, based on 
	the following processing steps. 
	(1) Download from EDGAR: Download 10-K files from EDGAR using Perl. 
	(2) Process text: Process text using Perl to gather identifying information, count of numbers, market float,
	and fog score. First, separate header information (cik, company name, industry).
	Exclude exhibit portion of filings (XML, GIFs) and keep only <html> or <text> portions. Use elinks to strip 
	html from document, then change html-coded characters to plain text and eliminate redundant spaces/tabs/dashes/dots. 
	Parse filing into individual MD&A, financial statement (FS), and footnote (FN) sections in four different 
	(successively less restrictive) ways: Round 1, capture MD&A and FS headings from Table of Contents based on 
	Item 7/VII/seven and 8/VIII/eight designations, and, if reasonable length headings found (<300 characters), 
	search for clean versions of headings (i.e., exclude related page numbers and extra spaces) in body of 
	filing with Item 7 (MDA) or 8 (FS) before the heading. Then separate Item 8 into actual FS and FN using 
	regular expressions for typical headings (e.g., for FS, consolidated/combined statement of 
	income/operations/financial condition/earnings in different ordering and with optional terms; for FN, notes 
	accompanying/to the combined/consolidated financial statements or footnote 1/one summary of 
	significant accounting policies or basis of presentation). Round 2, search for typical MDA, FS, and FN headings 
	in the filing using Item numbers as well (rather than relying on table of contents, making sure not to capture 
	references to section or table of contents, and making sure to search for end of footnotes based on item 9 or 
	10 changes in/disagreements with or directors, executive officers, and corporate governance). Round 3, search 
	in filing based on typical section headings without item numbers. Round 4, search in filing for just FS and FN based on 
	typical section headings and allowing for short additional phrases in the middle or end of heading. For each firm, 
	choose the first round that has	values for all three sections. If none exist, then choose the first round that has 
	values for both FS and FN. Details for how numbers and market float are captured are detailed below.

evidence.description: The footnote input is an XBRL-US-derived table with text, descriptions and Perl-counted statistics.
evidence.quote:
dxbrl.raw_extra_footnotes - Provides statistics on block-tagged XBRL footnote data for each firm filing, with footnote text
	along with footnote description pulled from XBRL US database based on the term "TextBlock" included in the element description, 
	and Perl code used to count the number of numbers in each footnote, using the same regular expression as the main tags_notes variable.

evidence.description: Active SAS code generates the Compustat intermediate using five prior fiscal years and constructs analyst coverage from Compustat and IBES.
The final variable-generation and sample-filter block is Stata code embedded inside the SAS document comment; it is not a standalone driver.
evidence.quote:
/**Additional data cleaning and creation performed in STATA before regression analyses;

// Final variable creation and naming //
gen tag_ratio_notes = num_tags_notes / num_tags_all
gen tag_ratio_fs 	= num_tags_fs / num_tags_all
gen analyst 		= numanalysts
replace analyst 	= 0 if analyst==.
replace inst_hold	= 0 if inst_hold==.
replace numsegments = 0 if numsegments==.
gen lnwords 		= ln(num_words_notes)
gen lnanalyst		= ln(1+analyst)
gen lnown			= ln(cshr)
gen lnsegments		= ln(1+numsegments)
gen lnmv			= ln(mv)
gen lnretvol		= ln(py_ret_std)
gen lntags 			= ln(num_tags_notes)
**Dropping observations where tag count ratios suggest meaningful data collection errors /// 
			(i.e., very few or no numbers in financial statements, no words in footnotes)
replace num_tags_notes=. if num_tags_notes<15 | num_tags_fs<15 | num_tags_fs==. | ///
			num_tags_all<15 | num_tags_all==. | fog_notes==. | fog_notes==0 | num_words_notes==. | num_words_notes ==0  ///
			| tag_ratio_notes<.02 | tag_ratio_notes>.85 | tag_ratio_fs<.005 | tag_ratio_fs>.75
replace lntags=. if num_tags_notes==.
** Identifying if required variables are there
gen reqvar = 1
foreach x in at roa py_abn_ret ev_chg_ib_ps py_ret_std mtb lnanalyst lnown lnmv lnsegments lnretvol {
	replace reqvar=0 if `x'==.
}
keep if reqvar==1

evidence.description: The author identifies historical XBRL-US tag data and several WRDS financial products used.
evidence.quote:
XBRL Filing Status and Tag Details: I obtained a listing of all XBRL filings with the SEC
   from a database created and hosted by XBRL US (https://xbrl.us/) (available to all paying
   members) approximately July 2011 (for filings from 2006 through 2010), August 2013 (for
   filings from 2011 through 2012) and January 2016 (for filings after 2012). I then processed
   the list using SAS to delineate basic from detailed filing status. I also obtained detailed
   XBRL tag information for the footnote disaggregation analysis during August 2013.

   Historical Financial Information: I obtained firm, capital market, analyst, and institutional
   holdings information from the Compustat (Annual, Quarterly, and Segments), CRSP, IBES,
   and Thomson Reuter’s Institutional Holdings databases via WRDS during August 2013,
   January 2016, and May 2018. At the same time, I also obtained CIK-CUSIP links from both
   Compustat and CRSP for use in linking the CIK from SEC filings to the historical
   information from Compustat and CRSP.

evidence.description: The appendix describes additional analyses but does not provide their executable programs.
evidence.quote:
This internet appendix contains additional analyses referenced in the main document.

Section IA1. Alternative Control Variable and Model Specifications

        I repeat my main analyses with adjustments to variable and model specifications to
provide comfort that results are not driven by a specification choice. All panels provide results of
estimating model 1, with adjustments as detailed. Coefficients are provided with t-statistics in
parentheses below, except for Panel F where standard errors are provided in parentheses. All
models have firm-clustered, robust standard errors. Variables are as defined in Appendix D of
the manuscript and are winsorized at 1% and 99%. The reported R-squared is from “within”
estimation (i.e., does not include the effect of firm fixed effects). ***, **, * Significantly
different from zero at the 1%, 5%, and 10% (two-tailed) level or better, respectively.

dxbrl.raw_shrcd - Provides share code from crspq.stocknames.

evidence.description: The author documents CIK/GVKEY and CIK/CUSIP links, filing matches, manual corrections and XBRL adoption/tag classification.
evidence.quote:
**Linking to compustat: Download cik/gvkey link based on crspq.comphist, and cik/gvkey/permno link from CRSP. Backfill CRSP 
	start date of cik match to 1/1/2004 if start date is 4/14/2007 (earliest available date) as assumption to get 
	coverage for  2006. Manually review fiscal period end or market float for outliers that are data errors and correct 
	mistakes. Match SEC filing to compustat/crsp year end based on cik and fiscal period end near compustat/crsp fiscal 
	period end, using CRSP match first then compustat match if no CRSP match. Remove duplicate gvkey-cik matches, 
	choosing those with CRSP as match source, market float available, or a longer history of matching.  
	If SEC filing has multiple cik's, keep the one that matches the best source and has largest asset value. 
	(3) Match to XBRL data: Match with tag count information pulled from XBRL US database to determine adoption status.
	Per firm filing, XBRL includes total distinct numeric tags, and distinct numeric tags by presentation section 
	[(statement, disclosure, document) where section is determined based on the presentation arc for the tag 
	having the first word equal to statement, disclosure, or document, or related section words in the description 
	(statement, balance sheet, balance s, balancce sheet, results of operations, and disclosure/schedule of 
	parenthetical data to/for the condensed/consolidated balance sheets/statements of cash flows/income for the
	Statement section, schedule and details for Disclosure, and entity information for Document]. Matched based 
	on SEC accession number first, then cik and fiscal period if no accession number matches. If still no match, 
	adjust XBRL fiscal period end to exactly one year prior to future filing or one year after
	prior filing to see if fiscal period end data entry error. Identify detail(basic) tagging adopters as those with 
	more (fewer) than 30 disclosure tags. Set Tier1, Tier2 and Tier3 designations using market float cutoffs 
	($5 billion, $700 million), then manually adjust for fiscal year end differences or timing that result in different 
	first adoption years to ensure that firms are classified in the correct category.

evidence.description: Active SAS code joins the prepared filing panel to generated Compustat/IBES tables, segments, ownership, CRSP share codes and a one-year filing-date return window.
The footnote consumer joins on accession ID and reads element name, namespace, tag/word counts and description, then keeps the largest filing-element record.
evidence.quote:
proc sql; create table fdetail as select distinct a.filingid, b.element_name, 
		CASE when lowcase(b.namespace) contains 'us-gaap' then 1 else 0 end as std_element,
		b.namespace, b.num_tags as num_tags_footnote, b.num_words as num_words_footnote
	from dxbrl.final as a join dxbrl.raw_extra_footnotes as b
		on a.accession_id_xbrl=b.accession_id and a.accession_id_xbrl ne .
			and (lowcase(b.description) contains "disclosure" | lowcase(b.description) contains "schedule") 
				and lowcase(b.description) not contains "(tables)"
				and lowcase(b.description) not contains "(table)" and lowcase(b.description) not contains "(policy)"
				and lowcase(b.description) not contains "(detail)" and lowcase(b.description) not contains "(details)"
				and index(lowcase(b.element_name),"tabletextblock")=0 
				and index(lowcase(b.element_name),"reconciliation") ne 1
	order by a.filingid, b.element_name, b.num_tags desc;quit;
**Use biggest footnote if there are duplicate records per filingid and element to take parent company;
proc sort data=fdetail nodupkey; by filingid element_name;run;

evidence.description: The Stata block creates scaled variables with the SCall_ prefix.
evidence.quote:
**Generating scaled variable
gen year_scale = 0
foreach var in num_tags_notes lntags lntags_nonzero num_tags_notes_nonzero lnwords ///
	fog_notes lnanalyst inst_hold lnown lnmv lnsegments roa py_abn_ret ev_chg_ib_ps lnretvol mtb {
		sort permno xyear
		by permno: egen temp1 = mean(`var')
		gen SCall_`var' = `var' / temp1
		replace SCall_`var' = 0 if `var'==0 & temp1==0
		drop temp1
}

evidence.description: Later Stata difference variables read SC* names and winsorize the specified variables at one percent.
evidence.quote:
*Create difference variables for percent change and scaled tags variable
sort permno xyear
gen Dnum_tags_notes = D.num_tags_notes if (xbrl1==1 & xyear>=2010) | (xbrl2==1 & xyear>=2011) | (xbrl3==1 & xyear>=2012)
sort permno xyear
gen DPnum_tags_notes = D.SCnum_tags_notes if (xbrl1==1 & xyear>=2010) | (xbrl2==1 & xyear>=2011) | (xbrl3==1 & xyear>=2012)
local vars "total cc comp ma other pension seg tax debt der gia pol ppe qtr seq fv sec rec"
foreach y of local vars {
	gen Dtagsa_`y' = D.tagsa_`y' if (xbrl1==1 & xyear>=2010) | (xbrl2==1 & xyear>=2011) | (xbrl3==1 & xyear>=2012)
	gen DPtagsa_`y' = D.SCtagsa_`y' if (xbrl1==1 & xyear>=2010) | (xbrl2==1 & xyear>=2011) | (xbrl3==1 & xyear>=2012)
}

// Winsorize //
foreach x in num_tags_notes num_tags_fs tag_ratio_notes tag_ratio_fs num_words_notes ///
	num_tags_notes_nonzero lntags lntags_nonzero fog_notes mkt_float at analyst ///
	lnwords lnmv lnanalyst lnown lnsegments lnretvol inst_hold cshr numsegments roa ///
	py_abn_ret ev_chg_ib_ps py_ret_std mtb num_footnotes mv ///
	num_der_hedge num_fi num_sec_vie num_fv tfva tfva_ratio {
		winsor `x', gen(temp) p(.01)
		replace `x'=temp
		drop temp
}
foreach x of varlist tagsa_* lntagsa_* wordsa_* ln_wordsa_* Dtagsa_* ///
	DPtagsa_* Dnum_tags_notes DPnum_tags_notes SCall* {
		winsor `x', gen(temp) p(.01)
		replace `x'=temp
		drop temp
}

evidence.description: The embedded Stata fragment ends at the closing SAS block-comment delimiter and is not a standalone Stata entry program.
The historical SEC preparation used Perl for filing text/section measures and manual checks through the graphical SEC EDGAR interface.
evidence.quote:
SEC Filing Information: The 10-K reports were downloaded from the SEC’s EDGAR index
   website (ftp://ftp.sec.gov/) on an approximately monthly basis from August 2013 and
   forward. I cleaned and processed the filings using a Perl script to first obtain basic firm
   information, basic filing information, and the market float. I identified the financial
   statements section and the footnote section using Perl, and I then used a Perl script to count
   the number of quantitative disclosures, count the number of words, calculate the fog score of
   each section, and capture the number of mentions for certain words (i.e., financial instrument,
   fair value, etc.). I also obtained examples and manually checked firm XBRL status and
   market float for some filings via the graphical SEC EDGAR interface throughout the study’s
   timeframe.

evidence.description: The datasheet also lists EDGAR download logs and SEC disclosure-focus materials; these are not consumed by the supplied SAS/embedded preparation code.
evidence.quote:
EDGAR Downloads: The logs of user access of EDGAR filings were downloaded from the
   SEC’s website (https://www.sec.gov/data/edgar-log-file-data-set) during January 2016.

   SEC Disclosure Focus: I captured the information to estimate the SEC’s disclosure focus
   during the time period from the following sources: annual slide presentations of the “Current
   Developments in the Division of Corporate Finance” from
   http://www.sec.gov/News/Page/List/Page/1356125649549 and audit firm executive
   summaries of SEC comment letters from Ernst and Young’s website and Deloitte Touche’s
   website.
